text:
maria: FYI customer Jules reported intermittent 502/504s during a canary rollout around 2026-03-10T15:40Z. They included request id req-0a1b2c3d. Quote: "generation failed mid-stream". Can we repro? I'll attach logs shortly.

alex: Thanks. Can you paste the full request id and a sample curl? Also which model pin did the customer set?

jules: request id req-0a1b2c3d. We pinned to redwood/gpt-xl:2026-03-09 (stable). Canary rollout was redwood/gpt-xl:2026-03-10-canary. We saw fallback to redwood/gpt-xl:2025-12-quant in response headers.

ingrid: Hmm, that mismatch could explain things. Fallback should pick a compatible variant but not older architecture. Can you share response headers and the X-Request-Id trace?

maria: headers: x-req-id=req-0a1b2c3d, x-model-variant=redwood/gpt-xl:2025-12-quant, x-fallback-reason=capacity_shortage, x-route=region-us-west-1.pool-burst

alex: SRE - can you repro with a curl? Customer provided this sanitized curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-xl:2026-03-09","input":"<sample prompt>","max_tokens":256}'``` They saw a 502 after ~1-2s then a 200 with a different model in the subsequent response.

ryan: I'll try to reproduce against a dedicated pool with the same model pin. Also need the debug bundle from their session. @maria can you request the debug bundle (run `ri-debug collect --reqid req-0a1b2c3d --include-kvcache --out=jules-bundle.tar` and share the upload)?

maria: Sent instructions to Jules; they uploaded jules-bundle.tar to s3://redwood-support/jules/1769956789. Link (internal): https://s3.redwood/support/jules/1769956789 (private).

ingrid: Once we have the bundle, I'll check kernel selection logs and kv-cache miss patterns. If the canary introduced a new attention kernel, fallbacks to a quantized variant may be causing a mismatch in streaming/chunking logic.

alex: Also capturing control-plane decision logs: route-policy=cost-optimized, fallback-policy=compatible-variant, canary-weight=10%. I suspect pool pressure -> fallback to lower-cost quantized variant which doesn't support the same streaming semantics.

maria: Customer says there was no billing spike or auth failure. They did hit some 429s earlier in the hour but those were unrelated. They saved the raw response body: ```{"error":"upstream: broken pipe","request_id":"req-0a1b2c3d"}```

ryan: Repro plan: (1) replay their curl against a canary node with the same pool config, (2) capture per-token latency + server logs, (3) force fallback to quant variant and reproduce streaming failure. Will run this on a mirrored infra and update here in ~2 hours.

ingrid: If we confirm a kernel/streaming incompatibility, we should pause this canary rollout and roll it back. Also consider updating routing rules to disallow fallback for streaming endpoints until variants are verified.

maria: Thanks all — alerted the account team and marked this as urgent. Will post updates as soon as Ryan has repro evidence. :thumbsup:
